content:
Some news it seems via the wire: https://blog.zulip.com/2026/05/15/announcing-zulip-foundation/

Congratulations!
Exciting but tbh I'm kinda scared that those super important people are leaving without replacement (unless I missed something)
This is the most depressing news I've seen in a long time. It seems we should really try hard to enjoy Zulip before AI enshittification starts.

Are you worried that Anthropic is indirectly in the board now? To me it reads like they won't let it happen, it sounds like Zulip was a passion project and handing it off to a foundation before moving to Anthropic is intended to avoid just that. (but maybe I'm naive and this is an acquisition in disguise :see_no_evil:)

I’m stepping back from Zulip to join Anthropic because of its remarkable commitment to the responsible development of AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

I found this part rather peculiar.
Oh ? Seems like standard LinkedIn dialect to me

Chris C said:

Oh ? Seems like standard LinkedIn dialect to me

I guess I also mean the part after it, and in fact the entire "Why I’m stepping back from full-time Zulip leadership" part.

Because it seems a bit dogmatic and intense, the reason for leaving full-time Zulip leadership is seemingly a deep felt sense of responsibility in the face of the paradigm shattering AI wrecking-ball.

And that Anthropic is our saviour, rather than the active cause of it, and there is just a responsibility to use their mind for the good of the human race through Anthropic.

I suppose i expected that section to be more about Zulip or maybe looking to change career, looking for a challenge , or some other generic bland reason ( could just be a lot more pay ).

Patrick Massot said:

This is the most depressing news I've seen in a long time. It seems we should really try hard to enjoy Zulip before AI enshittification starts.

I don't know what in the post makes you think AI enshittification is a plausible outcome of our setting up an independent Zulip Foundation to steward Zulip, with a lot of thoughtful people on the board. It is not.

I know the world is a place where companies constantly misbehave. But the main reason we are setting up the Zulip Foundation is to ensure Zulip remains a values-focused project permanently. A central part of its mission going forward is providing an excellent experience to public-benefit projects like Lean community.

So cheer up! This is a very good thing if you don't want Zulip to ever be enshittified.

Are you worried that Anthropic is indirectly in the board now?

Just to be clear, that's not how nonprofit boards work. Anthropic has no authority over the Zulip Foundation whatsoever. As far as I know, they have no reason to want Zulip enshittified; certainly everyone there who I've spoken with has been quite supportive of my efforts to make sure Zulip has a promising future as an independent non-profit.

And everyone who knows me can tell you I am the kind of person who would quit if my employer tried to direct my actions as the board member of a charitable foundation.

Let me clarify a couple of points:

  • Although I’m an administrator of this Zulip instance, I’m not speaking on behalf of the community, only expressing my personal worries.
  • So far our experience with Zulip has been amazing. I’m extremely grateful for the incredible work you and your team have put into Zulip and supporting its users. The success of Lean and its user community may have been impossible without Zulip.
  • Since a couple of months, moderators of this instance had a really hard time fighting AI slop. We had to setup a bot to help use manage temporary bans. Almost every day we suspend several accounts because of AI. This is really time and human energy consuming.
  • I find it incredibly hard to believe that having so many Zulip leaders moving to work at Anthropic won’t result in Zulip getting new AI “features” that will help people post more slop more easily, or help AI companies who want to steal our work by training on our conversations here. I would love to be proven wrong.
Also, I didn’t mean I think your new employer will try to force you doing this, I fear that your will to work for an AI company means you’ll happily do it without being forced to.

I agree with Patrick here. It is highly concerning that Tim announces

The foundation’s initial board of directors will be:

  • Tim Abbott
  • Greg Price
  • Alya Abbott
  • Josh Triplett

and then later writes,

Three additional members of Zulip’s longtime leadership team are also joining me at Anthropic: Alya Abbott, Greg Price, and Alex Vandiver.

That means 3/4 of the Zulip Foundation board of directors are working for Anthropic :grimacing:

Tim also states that the Zulip Foundation is

similar to governance structures for Mozilla, Signal, and Wikipedia

I am not familiar with Mozilla or Signal, but Wikipedia has very strict rules about conflict of interest which would explicitly forbid this sort of thing. Wikipedia's Board of Trustees is also majority run by community members. The last election was in 2024 and had over 6000 voters. Zulip would be wise to copy these policies.

Patrick Massot said:

  • Since a couple of months, moderators of this instance had a really hard time fighting AI slop. We had to setup a bot to help use manage temporary bans. Almost every day we suspend several accounts because of AI. This is really time and human energy consuming.

Yeah I hate AI slop too. We've had a similar experience at a lesser scale with contributors to zulip/zulip on GitHub since circa November, and it has been very challenging and pushed our processes away from some things we loved to do with new people. I've been pretty happy with our AI usage policy banning AI in communication with humans.

The Zulip 12.0 blog post had a screen-tall section about this experience. If folks have ideas for tools Zulip could build that would help manage these issues in Zulip communities, I expect there would be interest. (Maybe we can brainstorm in a separate topic).

I believe that it is possible to do valuable non-slop work with AI, but it currently requires a lot of understanding and steering from a person who knows what they are doing. (I've gotten a lot of value out of audits for various classes of bugs in recent months, and in general feel pretty good about efficacy for search problems that are then verified unambigiously by the human who is using the tool before sharing with anyone else. For example, two weeks ago, I did an audit for accidentally quadratic bugs in the Zulip web app that I think everyone will appreciate having been fixed).

Overall though, the design philosophy of Zulip has been a research project into finding the best human-computer interface for people to have complex collections of conversations together, and having the 3 people who have been driving the product design for Zulip for the last decade on the initial board is the right way to preserve stability of vision.

I will say, there are a few AI features that I could see being nice in Zulip, for example a flow wherein you can have an LLM "Suggest a topic" after writing the body of a message might be helpful, if very carefully and thoughtfully integrated. A lot of people find it hard to figure out what a good topic is, and I'm not sure an LLM can do that well, but "make it easier to come up with a topic" has been a perennial feature request since before LLMs were invented.

The main work we've historically done in the area of AI features is beta work on a "summarize this topic" button, more than a year ago, that we did not ship, which entailed a lot of planning around how to make it easy for users to disable AI features at various levels.

The world is changing, and I can't say what AI features Zulip's maintainers will decide to merge; I don't expect to be making those decisions if things are going well. But what I can say is I think everyone's goal is to continue Zulip's design philosophy wherein the goal is to help people have better conversations, and we'd be horrified if changes we made had as a major effect or side effect causing people to post more slop.

Zulip has never had any "make metric go up" engagement hacking optimization efforts. I think one needs to be incredibly careful with that sort of thing with this class of product, because given a fixed amount of conversations you need to have, more messages and time in that community can be a signal that your conversation is working less well.
